1	// Part: room: guest bath. A 3 x 7 bath, inner air x35..37 z54..60, floor row y4, lit from above.
2	// Focal piece: a three-cell water tub along the far (south) wall, in view from the door at z53 x36.
3	// Vanity on the east wall at the near end: a planks cabinet (two cells) with a basin cauldron and a flower pot on top.
4	// A barrel for linen by the west wall at the near end.
5	// Lane: x36 z54..59 stays clear from the door to the tub and the vanity; x35 z55..57 stays clear for the west doorways.
6	import { layers } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/build.mjs";
7	
8	export function build(g) {
9	  const legend = {
10	    B: "barrel",
11	    C: "dark_oak_planks",
12	    S: "cauldron",
13	    F: "flower_pot",
14	    W: ["water_cauldron", { level: "3" }],
15	    L: ["lantern", { hanging: "true" }],
16	    M: ["lantern", { hanging: "false" }],
17	  };
18	  // rows run along +x (x35, x36, x37), successive rows along +z (z54 .. z60)
19	  layers(g, [35, 4, 54], legend, [
20	    [
21	      // y4: floor row, stand row
22	      "B C", // z54: linen barrel west, cabinet east
23	      "  C", // z55: cabinet second block
24	      "   ", // z56
25	      "   ", // z57
26	      "   ", // z58
27	      "   ", // z59
28	      "WWW", // z60: the tub along the south wall
29	    ],
30	    [
31	      // y5: on the cabinet top
32	      "M S", // z54: standing lantern on the linen barrel (x35), basin on the cabinet (x37); x36 stays clear
33	      "  F", // z55: flower pot
34	    ],
35	  ]);
36	  // hanging lantern over the tub, under the upper floor at y10
37	  layers(g, [36, 9, 59], legend, [["L"]]);
38	}
39

content.text: The lock is the cause. The shell carves the whole interior to air with `fill(..., "air")`, and `runParts` treats every cell an earlier part wrote, air included, as owned. I'll confirm which bath cells the shell owns before deciding how to proceed.

The shell's `box()` carves every interior cell to air, and the partitions and floors own the rest. So every cell in the bath is owned by an earlier part, and no cell here is free for `room-7` to write into. I'll confirm the rest of the lock with a run after the edit. The sanctioned fix is to remove the refused writes, so I'll take them out and keep the drawn layout in comments so it can come back once the shell stops locking carved air.

input.summary:
room-7 guest bath: the REFUSED writes are removed from parts/room-7.mjs, so the bath has no fit-out (tub, vanity, linen barrel, lanterns); the layout is kept in comments.
make.sh now shows neither REFUSED nor OFF-PALETTE for this part (it has no off-palette blocks); build.nbt is written.
Root cause is outside this file: the shell's box() carves room air to "air" (parts/shell.mjs:27) and runParts locks every cell an earlier part wrote, so no room part can place anything.
left: The guest bath is not furnished. The three-cell water tub, vanity cabinet, linen barrel, flower pot and lanterns were all refused, so I removed them; their coordinates are kept as comments in parts/room-7.mjs.

Root cause is in parts/shell.mjs:27: box() carves the whole room interior to air, and runParts locks every cell an earlier part wrote, air included. Every room part in this build is blocked the same way, not only this one. The fix belongs in the shell or in runParts (leave room air unlocked, or run the room parts before the carve); I did not edit other modules.
Once the lock is fixed, restore the layout from the comment in room-7.mjs: y4 barrel and planks at x35/x37 z54..55, water_cauldron tub at z60 x35..37, y5 lantern, cauldron and flower pot.
Not this part's problem, reported by the same run: roof.json puts off-palette blocks into the roof (tuff_bricks, tuff_brick_slab, cobbled_deepslate_stairs and others). Left for the roof owner.
The REFUSED report lists only the first 8 of the 10 refused writes, so the count was only visible from the part line.

waste.what: Finding out why the writes were refused: I read build.mjs's runParts lock, shell.mjs's box() carve and the parts-report.json by hand to confirm that the shell owns every cell in the bath.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls and one full make.sh run (38 parts) to see the refusals, plus reading two modules
waste.tool: A pre-flight in runParts or mcd plan that prints each part's footprint and how many cells are already owned, e.g. 'room: guest bath: 0 of 10 cells free (shell owns the room air)', so the cause shows before any build run.

waste.what: The REFUSED report caps its list at 8 entries (refusedAt.slice(0, 8)), so the 10th refused write was invisible and the count had to be inferred.
waste.cost: one extra reasoning step to count the layers() writes against the refused total
waste.tool: Report every refused cell, or give the total with a pointer to the full list in parts-report.json.

waste.what: Hand-deleting furniture writes and re-commenting the layout, which an explicit 'remove or move' edit did with no way to move them to a free cell.
waste.cost: one Write of the 38-line file, with the layout retyped as comments
waste.tool: A runParts option (or layers() flag) that marks a part's cells as unlocked when the carve is the shell's own, so room fit-out can land in carved air without editing the shell.
